facts.text: Founded in 1827, Shullsburg is one of the oldest settlements in Wisconsin and was established through early lead mining ventures.
Shullsburg is where the term Badgers was first coined to describe local lead miners, later becoming the official mascot for the University of Wisconsin.
The Water Street Commercial District in Shullsburg features thirty-four buildings listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Shullsburg is located within the Midwestern Driftless Area and is well known for its history of lead mining and its cheese industry.
Missionary Priest Samuel Mazzuchelli platted the northeast section of Shullsburg in 1841 and named the streets after the virtues of life.
Badger Park in Shullsburg was completed in 1942 by the Works Progress Administration and features a baseball park with lights.
